item.title: Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US
item.description: TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn't allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US. The Trump administration imposed a sweeping ban on foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn't been able to obtain an exemption. The rules prevent the import or sale of all new router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US. The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security. While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials. Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but its newly released Wi-Fi 8 routers cannot be imported or sold. Read full article Comments

item.title: Tiger Woods ‘Still Fully Believes’ He Can ‘Beat Anyone’ at Golf Despite ‘Dealing With So Much Pain’
item.description: ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA Tiger Woods wants to be a champion — and anything less is going to be very hard for him to accept as he prepares to return to the world of professional golf at the Hero World Challenge tournament in the Bahamas in December, a source tells Globe . “Even with everything that’s happened, Tiger still fully believes he can, and will, beat anyone on the course,” reveals the source. “It’s a great mindset, but it’s also worrying because a lot of people think he’s setting the bar too high.” Over the years, Woods, 50, has sustained several injuries, per AP , including a ruptured Achilles tendon and ACL, and undergone multiple back surgeries. As Globe previously reported, the 82-time PGA Tour champion also recently completed a stint in rehab in Switzerland after rolling over his Land Rover in Jupiter, Florida, on March 27. He was charged with a DUI but pleaded no contest to a lesser charge that will see his driver’s license suspended for five years. “His body just isn’t what it used to be,” admits the source. “He’s still dealing with so much pain. Everyone is telling him that just making this comeback is incredible, regardless of whether he wins or not, but Tiger doesn’t want to hear that.” Instagram/Tiger Woods Girlfriend Vanessa Trump is “very supportive, but she also doesn’t want to see him overdo it or get down on himself if things don’t go his way,” says Globe ‘s source. At the same time, “she’s also got to protect her own peace,” the source adds. In late October, Donald Trump Jr. ‘s ex-wife, 48, announced on Instagram that she is officially cancer-free after undergoing treatment for cancer earlier this year. “She’s been through so much with her health,” notes the source. “She needs her life to be as stress-free as possible and that is going to be hard if Tiger’s putting all this pressure on himself.” Read More From Globe Professor Who Claims His Affair With a Student Was Like 'Fatal Attraction' Accused of Sexual Assault Man Named Captain America Accused of Murdering Coworker, Demanding Money From His Girlfriend Kentucky Teacher Charged With 30 New Counts of Abuse, Human Trafficking of Minors After Prior Arrests This story Tiger Woods ‘Still Fully Believes’ He Can ‘Beat Anyone’ at Golf Despite ‘Dealing With So Much Pain’ first appeared on Globe . item.title: GB's Davis Cup-winning captain ends 17-year stint
item.description: Leon Smith guided Great Britain to their first Davis Cup title in 79 years [Getty Images] Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith is stepping down after almost 17 years in the role. Smith guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936. The 50-year-old Scot will leave his role after next week's Finals in Bologna, where he is hoping to create "another special memory" by leading the team to the title once again. Smith's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible. Former world number one Andy Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 victory, is not believed to be interested in the role at this time. "It has been an enormous privilege to lead the team for so many years, and I feel now is the right time, both for me personally and for the team moving forwards," Smith said. "Winning the Davis Cup in 2015 will always be one of the proudest moments of my career, but there are countless other experiences and memories that I'll cherish forever." With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign. Murray was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career. "He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play. He got the best out of us that year," three-time Grand Slam champion Murray said. "I've obviously known Leon a long time, I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments. "I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain." Smith, who took over the role in 2010, is Britain's longest-serving Davis Cup captain [Getty Images] Live scores, results and order of play Get tennis news sent straight to your phone

item.title: Puka Nacua faces NFL ‘banishment’ under suspension guidelines
item.description: Before Week 11 of the 2026-27 NFL season kicked off, the league announced that one of its biggest stars, Puka Nacua , has been suspended for three games for violating the personal conduct policy . The timing of the suspension turned out to be beneficial to the Rams and Nacua. Nacua is currently on injured reserve, so he was set to miss the next three games regardless of his status with the league. The All-Pro pass catcher will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, December 14 . However, Nacua’s suspension does come with a strong warning from the league. NFL Insider Tom Pelissero shared further details about what any future violation or “failure to satisfy conditions of the diversion program” could entail. According to Pelissero, if Nacua does not comply with the diversion program or finds himself in trouble down the road, it “could lead to additional discipline, up to and including banishment .” MORE: Stephen A. Smith still holding out hope for Rams’ Super Bowl run Puka Nacua Suspension Must Be Wake-up Call Oct 18, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) warms up before the game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) At just 25 years old, Nacua has a long career ahead of him if he can stay healthy and out of trouble. The good news is Nacua voluntarily entered a holistic care and recovery facility in Malibu as his off-field issues began to pile up. “I feel like I’ve learned is it’s OK to ask for support,” Nacua said after his first stint in the rehab facility. “Little did I know that even just writing in a journal, as simple as that, and finding ways to express some of the things I have near and dear to my heart … it’s been a great improvement in my life.” With such a bright future ahead of him, let’s hope that Nacua continues to improve off the field and reflect on some of the mistakes he made. He will also have to use that time to continue rehabbing his knee (PCL/MCL sprain) and turf toe injuries suffered in Week 9. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Does Villanova Basketball Have A Backcourt Problem?
item.description: Villanova has played just five games and there have been some strong reactions to the overall performance. Is it too early to make judgments and overreact? The answer is no. When a team rebuilds a roster that cost plenty of money, results are expected right away. Let’s not forget, in five games, Villanova has played two real opponents and have lost both games. With Michigan and Kansas coming up, it could get uglier if the team does not clean up. The main issue that needs to get cleaned up is in the backcourt. The point guard position has not been good enough. Elijah Crawford has made some plays early this season, particularly against Notre Dame in the opener, but it is becoming clear that he has not been good enough. Is it quick to say that he is not good enough to play in the Big East? That is yet to be seen, but the early returns have not been positive. Crawford was a big-time recruit coming out of high school before going to BYU and then UIC. He is not going to be asked to score much for Villanova. He is averaging six assists through five games with 2.2 turnovers. It is important that the team has a ball handler to set the offense up with what should be an improved frontcourt and Tyler Perkins on the perimeter. Darryl Simmons was also added this offseason. He has been a strong shooter from deep during his career. This is a valuable skillset off the bench. Simmons is already dealing with an injury that kept him sidelined against Pitt. We’re not going to mention how both Acaden Lewis and Bryce Lindsay are off to strong starts for their respective teams this season. We’re not going to do it. But if we were to, how different would it look? There is some time before Big East play begins. That is what really matters for Villanova. But to compete this year, the backcourt must get figured out.

item.title: Tottenham Hotspur vs. Ipswich Town Premier League Preview
item.description: It was a shockingly positive October for Tottenham Hotspur with a draw at Old Trafford and three wins to follow, including the amazing result at Stamford Bridge. Of course, that naturally led to a depressingly flat performance against Leeds right before the break, which sent Spurs back to the bottom half of the table, though thankfully out of the relegation zone as has been the case for much of the past two seasons. Back in action, Tottenham gets three matches against teams below it in the table before a home North London Derby the first weekend of December. This run begins with a visit from Ipswich Town, who sits joint-13th with 11 points through 10 contests; all three of its wins this season came in the first six matchweeks, with just two points taken across the most recent four fixtures. Spurs disappointed against Leeds, but really must be taking all three points on Saturday. With back-to-back wins at home for the first time in ages, the Lane should be fully behind this squad against an overmatched opponent. Roberto De Zerbi’s group must take things one match at a time, but the next three matches feel like a quite important stretch. Match Details Date : Saturday, November 21 Time : 10:00 am ET, 3:00 pm UK Location : Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London TV : USA Network (US) Prior to Ipswich’s brief return to the Championship, these two sides split the contests in 2024/25, with the road team claiming each victory. In North London, the Tractor Boys scored twice in the first half, and a Rodrigo Bentancur consolation was not enough to prevent Ipswich from earning its first win. The reverse fixture saw four Spurs goals at Portman Road: a Brennan Johnson first-half brace, plus tallies from Djed Spence and Dejan Kulusevski to firmly put it away. Optimistically on the rise The rise in the table, the stringing together of wins, and the conquest over Chelsea all point to the tangible ways this team is making progress, and much of this felt overdue after Spurs kept putting together pieces of strong performances without being able to fully earn the result. The underlying metrics still see the club as squarely mid-table, but the trend is absolutely in the right direction. On top of this, optimism rises with the squad list. James Maddison, Savio, and Lucas Bergvall are among those who are coming back and should make a substantial impact in the lineup. With Kulusevski and Mohammed Kudus already available, De Zerbi will have far more attacking options now at his disposal, even with Mathys Tel and Xavi Simons out. This combination of form and personnel should have Tottenham’s confidence growing every week. Contrast that with the visitors who are winless in four and have only taken points from teams who are currently in the bottom eight spots of the table. Call me foolish, but this sets up well for Spurs, as the home side should be able to break down an opposing defense that has allowed the second-most goals this season. item.title: Morgan Gibbs-White x Harry Kane! Nottingham Forest star tipped to be on Bayern Munich’s transfer radar in 2027 as Jamal Musiala endures a tough time
item.description: Morgan Gibbs-White Bayern Munich crest 2026 - Getty/GOAL Could Morgan Gibbs-White link up with England international colleague Harry Kane at Bayern Munich in 2027? Dietmar Hamann has told GOAL why interest in the mercurial Nottingham Forest playmaker makes sense for the Bundesliga champions, with current No.10 Jamal Musiala having endured a tough time over the course of the last 18 months. Bayern will spend big on the right players With their standing in European and global games being taken into account, Bayern are forever in the market for elite performers with match-altering qualities. Historically, they have not been prepared to part with the biggest of fees - with reputation often working in their favour during transfer discussions. Purse strings have been loosened a little of late, with €100 million (£84m/$110m) being splashed out on former Tottenham striker Kane during the summer of 2023. Some €70m (£59m/$77m) was invested in Colombian forward Luis Diaz when prising him away from Liverpool, and €53m (£44m/$58m) on enigmatic France international winger Michael Olise. Value for money has been found in all of those deals. Olise has posted a remarkable tally of assists, Diaz is full of running down the flanks, while Kane - with 156 goals to his name through 162 appearances - has become a Ballon d’Or winner . England star Gibbs-White has seen stock soar There is always room for improvement, though, at the Allianz Arena and it has been suggested that another creative influence could be welcomed through the arrivals lounge. Speculation in the summer of 2026 hinted at Gibbs-White registering on the recruitment radar. He has become a talismanic presence for Forest, filling their captain’s armband on a regular basis, while earning 10 senior caps for the Three Lions . While boasting flicks and tricks aplenty, he is not a maverick No.10 and can always be relied upon to put in a shift that benefits the collective cause. Would Gibbs-White transfer make sense for Bayern? With that in mind, would MGW be a shrewd addition alongside Kane? When that question was put to Hamann, the former Bayern midfielder - who was speaking courtesy of Lottoland Live Casino - told GOAL : “In the forward department, they need to see. “Obviously, Musiala is out injured, he’s got his health problems. [Ismael] Saibari came to the club, didn't really start well, got injured now. So, I think in the forward positions, or in the attacking position, they've got to do something next summer. “I wouldn't be surprised if Gibbs-White is on the radar. He wouldn't be the only one. If I was a Forest fan, in a way I'd be happy that people are interested in my players because that means they're good players. “He seems to be very settled at Forest because he's kind of rejuvenated his career at Forest, done really well there. It would make sense, but I think we're a long way away from Gibbs-White coming to Munich.” Health concerns have hampered Musiala Bayern are mulling over their options after

item.title: #PostPulpit mailbag: What’s wrong with the Patriots defense?
item.description: Behind back-to-back blowout losses and losing Drake Maye to injury , the New England Patriots season has quickly derailed over the last two weeks. Now, they have plenty questions to answers after a much needed bye week. So, let’s get into some of those in this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. What has gone so wrong with the defense? They’re relatively healthy and have a lot of the same personnel as last year. Kuhr did a great job last year and really earned the official promotion to DC. So what happened? Along the same lines, do you think Gonzo is really the type of player who, now that he’s gotten his payday, is going to sit on his laurels for the remainder of his career? – TDDsDad Is the defense’s biggest problem the square peg or round hole – scheme doesn’t fit players or players don’t fit scheme – spyponder90 The Patriots defense has a litany of problems right now. Here’s how we’d break them down: Zone coverage: Statistically, the Patriots are the worst zone coverage team in football, ranking dead last in both EPA and passer rating allowed in zone coverage. Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr was a step ahead of opposing offenses earlier this season with his disguises in the secondary, but teams have caught on while New England’s defensive backs have failed to live up to their potential. Some of the issues in zone coverage also tie back to the pass rush. The Patriots rank 20th in the league in four-man pressure rate, giving opposing quarterbacks time to find the voids in coverage. To generate pressure, New England has had to blitz, which then leaves more space for the offense to attack with at least one defender taken out of coverage — as seen on Jahmyr Gibbs’ 50-yard reception last week. Man coverage: The logical follow-up would be to play more man coverage, especially with New England’s talented cover corners. The Patriots already rank near the top of the league in man coverage rate, but no team can rely on man coverage for the majority of a game for several reasons. Without an effective changeup, opposing offenses have game-planned for man coverage and exploit it with beaters such as stacks and bunch formations. On top of that, the talented cover corners have again not been playing to their potential. Effort/tackling: New England is not a poor tackling team by the numbers, but the defense often doesn’t appear to be rallying to the football — a concern when Mike Vrabel has made effort and finish his No. 1 non-negotiable . Opponents are piling up yards after the catch and yards after contact against New England. That reached a new low last week, when the Lions generated 220 yards after the catch and another 135 yards after contact on the ground. The effort doesn’t always show up on film, either. The defensive line allowed Detroit to average 4.5 yards before contact (!). Defenders in the secondary often take poor angles and seem more focused on ripping the ball out than getting the ball carrier to the ground. Coaching: Lastly, when it co

item.title: Arsenal has not forgotten about Brentford star ahead of January window
item.description: Arsenal has not forgotten about Brentford star ahead of January window Brentford star Kevin Schade has emerged as an attacker attracting Arsenal’s interest , with the Gunners reportedly adding him to their transfer target list . The German winger has been in impressive form in the Premier League and has established himself as an important member of the Brentford team. His performances have caught the attention of several top clubs, and Arsenal are among those monitoring his situation. They view Schade as an attacker who could fit into their squad and deliver strong performances if he makes the move to the Emirates Stadium. Schade has been particularly impressive for Brentford and appears to be improving with every season. His development has helped him attract interest, and Arsenal will hope he can continue progressing if they manage to bring him to the club. The winger is reportedly keen on the prospect of joining the Gunners, which could make a potential transfer worth exploring. Arsenal consider Schade an important transfer target The January transfer window could offer Arsenal an opportunity to act on their interest. The club are looking at ways to strengthen their attacking options , and Schade is understood to be among the players they would like to add to their squad. His ability to perform in the Premier League could make him an appealing option for the Gunners. However, any move would depend on Arsenal deciding to pursue a deal and Brentford’s willingness to consider losing one of their important players during the season. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) January move could be an option According to Caught Offside , Arsenal remain strongly interested in Schade and regard him as one of the most important names on their transfer shopping list. The report suggests the Gunners could make an effort to sign the German when the winter transfer window opens in January. Schade has been performing well for both club and country, and his form has put him on the radar of several leading sides. Arsenal will now have to decide whether to turn their interest into a formal approach. A move to the Emirates would give Schade the chance to take another step in his career, but he would also need to compete for a starting place. It remains to be seen whether Arsenal will make their move in January or whether the winger will continue his development at Brentford. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Shannon Sharpe thinks he knows ‘the main reason’ why LeBron James left the Lakers
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images LeBron James left the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2026 after eight years with the franchise. The 41-year-old joined the Philadelphia 76ers in the off-season, and he seems to be having a great time there. The Lakers are doing well without him too. Since his summer move, there have been several theories about why James decided to leave the Lakers. Shannon Sharpe has now had his say on what he thinks happened. Shannon Sharpe says LeBron James left the Lakers because he was disrespected James has been one of the biggest names in the NBA for a long time, and when he joined the Los Angeles Lakers, many expected them to dominate. However, the Lakers won just one NBA Championship with The King in his eight years there, which is one of the reasons why things turned a bit sour in the end. Some fans wanted James gone because they believed that Luka Doncic was their real star and would take them to the next level on his own. Sharpe believes that was one of the reasons why James felt disrespected and decided to leave. He said on the Nightcap show : “I think the main reason LeBron left the Lakers is that he felt like they didn’t respect him anymore. “He felt like, ‘Look, I understand Luka’s better, but y’all just blatantly disregarded what I’ve done for you guys the last eight years. Do y’all not remember what transpired the last couple of years Kobe was here? “‘Because Kobe was hurt a lot, and do you remember when Kobe retired, that 60-point game? What y’all did in ’16 and ’17. Do y’all remember that? And then for you to have this kind of laissez-faire attitude, it’s just like, you know what, y’all don’t really appreciate it.’ “And he heard it: ‘We don’t need LeBron. We don’t want LeBron. We got Luka.'” LeBron James’ summer departure has worked out for everyone There was a big debate in the summer following James’ departure from Los Angeles. Some were of the opinion that the Lakers would struggle this season, while others believed that The King’s new team, the Philadelphia 76ers, would have problems because of him. However, when you look at the records of the two teams, they are pretty similar. Of course, the debate about James and the Lakers will go on until the end of the season and perhaps even beyond that point. However, we think people should just accept that his departure was the best move for all parties involved and move on. item.title: Ben Shelton completes feat only Rafael Nadal can match this century after latest win at the ATP Finals
item.description: Ben Shelton broke new ground in his career by reaching the semifinals of the ATP Finals for the first time. After Arthur Fils lost the first set of his third and final group stage match against Alexander Zverev on Thursday, Shelton ‘s spot in the final four was confirmed. The 24-year-old American had beaten Rafael Jodar in straight sets earlier in the day to boost his chances of advancing at the prestigious year-end tournament. Photo by Pascal von Büren/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images Ben Shelton matches Rafael Nadal after advancing at the ATP Finals With his triumph, Shelton became the youngest American since Andy Roddick in 2004 to reach the semifinals of the ATP Finals. He also became the first left-hander other than Rafael Nadal to do so this century. Nadal made the semifinals six times and advanced to the championship match twice: in 2010 and 2013. The legendary Spaniard never managed to win the title, however, despite making 11 appearances. Shelton qualified for the ATP Finals for the first time last year, but was knocked out in the round-robin stage. He went winless in his debut campaign, winning just one set throughout the run against Felix Auger-Aliassime. This time around, Shelton has tallied a record of 2-1 in the group stage, having beaten Fils and Jodar but losing to Zverev. The loss to the German was his seventh straight in their head-to-head and first since the US Open final. Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images Ben Shelton’s semifinal opponent at the ATP Finals in Turin After finishing second in the John McEnroe group, Shelton will face the winner of the Ivan Lendl group, Carlos Alcaraz, on Monday. Alcaraz secured his spot atop his group after beating Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe, both in straight sets. Shelton has faced Alcaraz five times on the ATP Tour and has only come out on top against him once. Shelton’s sole victory in the head-to-head came in the quarterfinals of this year’s US Open, where he emerged victorious in a five-set thriller. Alcaraz has since earned revenge by beating Shelton in the Paris Masters final to extend his lead in the rivalry to 4-1. Their upcoming clash at the ATP Finals will be their third on an indoor hard court.

item.title: Celtic wonderkid scores stunning hat-trick for Scotland in 6-3 victory over Sweden
item.description: Celtic wonderkid scores stunning hat-trick for Scotland in 6-3 victory over Sweden Celtic youngster Lennon Watt continued his impressive goalscoring form with a hat-trick for Scotland U17s in their 6-3 victory over Sweden. The young Hoops striker was in outstanding form during the international clash in Tirana, Albania, adding another three goals to his growing tally. Watt has already established himself as one of Celtic’s most promising academy prospects, having scored an incredible 48 goals and registered 15 assists last season. His performances earned him a first professional contract at Parkhead during the summer, and he has since begun making the step up to Celtic’s B team. The teenager has already made six appearances at that level and is continuing to impress internationally, having also scored against Finland earlier in Scotland’s campaign. Fellow Celtic youngster Jacob Cameron was also involved in the victory over Sweden. The centre-back, who turned 16 just three months ago, has already broken into the Hoops’ B-team starting XI despite his young age. Watt’s hat-trick follows another impressive international contribution from Celtic’s academy, with Lucas Clearie recently finding the net for Scotland U19s against Belgium. item.title: 5 questions with the enemy ahead of Steelers-Eagles
item.description: Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers are looking to rebound this week as they head on the road to take on the 2-7 Eagles. We talked with Brandon Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation to figure out what’s gone wrong with Philadelphia’s season, and what we can expect for this game. 1. This Eagles roster is hardly recognizable from the squad that won the Super Bowl just two seasons ago. I think most fans are aware of the Jalen Hurts situation. Outside of that, can you summarize for Steelers fans what has gone wrong for the 2-7 Eagles this season? Brandon Gowton : For starters, I’d recommend checking out Jimmy Kempski’s “ Eagles season from hell ” tracker. The TL;DR version is that the Eagles have been really bad and injured. The new-look offense is even worse than it was last year … and it can’t just be blamed on injuries. The Eagles also looked bad on offense when they were healthy (see: the team scoring seven points in a Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears). The Eagles’ defense was supposed to be the strength of the team, but Vic Fangio’s unit has largely underwhelmed. Howie Roseman didn’t have a great offseason. In the past, the coaching staff really benefited from the Eagles’ general manager doing the heavy lifting. With the coaching staff now being required to do more with less, Nick Sirianni hasn’t been able to answer the bell. 2. It’s only been one game, but what can you tell us about the Joe Milton experience so far? What can we expect from him and from the offense in general this game? BG : It’s probably not going to be pretty for the Eagles. He’s inconsistent. He has the arm talent to make big throws. But his accuracy and touch were lacking in his first Eagles start. It was good to see the offense ran more vertical patterns than ever this season. But he didn’t actually take a lot of deep shots against the New York Giants. That might change this week, especially if DeVonta Smith and/or Dontayvion Wicks are able to return from injury. Milton’s mobility is also a nice element for the Eagles after watching Tanner McKee be a statue in the pocket. Philly leads the NFL in unblocked pressures this season. While it’s not ideal to often ask the QB to bail out the offensive line, it’s the reality the Eagles are currently facing. He might be able to run around a bit on Sunday. And if the Steelers’ defense has to respect that threat, Saquon Barkley could stand to benefit. But he’s probably just not going to play a very clean game. I expect sacks and turnovers. 3. The Eagles’ defense has seemingly slipped some this season, and the team just traded away Jordan Davis. What’s been happening on that side of the ball? How do you think that unit will play the Steelers? BG : The Eagles’ defense falling off is one of the bigger mysteries of this season. There was an expectation that this could be a top-five unit, if not challenge for the title of best defense in the NFL. This group clearly hasn’t come close to that standard. They have had som

item.title: With the No. 8 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft, the New York Liberty could address one of their biggest weaknesses
item.description: Breanna Stewart. | NBAE via Getty Images With the No. 8 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft, the New York Liberty will have the organization’s highest selection since 2022, when they owned the No. 5 pick (Nyara Sabally). Over the past four drafts, the Liberty have only had one other first-round pick, selecting at No. 11 overall in 2024 (Marquesha Davis). And of all the players on the 2026 Liberty roster, only three—Marine Fauthoux (No. 29, 2021), Sabrina Ionescu (No. 1, 2020) and Han Xu (No. 14, 2019)—were drafted by the franchise. The state of the New York roster reflects the superteam transformation that took place during the 2023 offseason, as well as the franchise’s subsequent championship-or-bust approach to every season, where the drafting and development of young players has been sacrificed in favor acquiring stars or veterans. It all, of course, paid off in 2024, when the Liberty captured that long-sought first championship. After finishing at No. 8 in the standings in 2026, New York now clings to their championship contender identity, as last offseason’s attempted refresh failed, leaving the currently head coach-less Liberty with questions about how to build a roster that capable of achieving the organization’s championship ambitions. Thank you, Coach DeMarco. pic.twitter.com/tbxe0MDInT — New York Liberty (@nyliberty) November 3, 2026 A singular middle-of-the-first-round draft pick doesn’t project to do much to alter the Liberty’s immediate future. And as tons of offseason activity will occur before draft night, there’s a decent chance New York, once again, might not be making this pick. However, the reality of the new CBA might change the Liberty’s team construction calculation. With all of Ionescu, Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones slated for max salaries in 2027, plus a more than $855,000 contract for Satou Sabally, New York could use contributors on cheaper contracts. So, presuming the Liberty are on the clock at No. 8 in April, can New York find a keeper who fills a need? Here’s a consideration of three approaches for New York. In the comments, give us your take on what the Liberty need, and if they can find it in the draft. New York could turn to South Carolina for win-now contributors Stewart and Jones remain one of, if not THE, best frontcourt tandems in the league. But, things get shaky behind Stewie and JJ, as Sabally’s health status after her extended struggles with concussions is still uncertain and Han, who comes with extreme offensive strengths and defensive weakness, is set to be a reserved free agent. Because of the two-way versatility of Stewart and Jones, players of a variety of archetypes are fits. For a team intent upon returning to contention, players that understand those expectations and, in turn, are willing do whatever’s needed to achieve that ambition should be priority. So, where better to find such prospects than Columbia, SC ? Chloe Kitts or Ashlyn Watkins would provide different flavors of frontcourt pop for the Lib

item.title: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. NC State Wolfpack
item.description: A view of the line of scrimmage with the Florida State Seminoles against the North Carolina State Wolfpack during the game at Doak Campbell Stadium on September 23, 2017 in Tallahassee, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Florida State Seminoles will attempt to become bowl-eligible for the first time since 2023 and wrap up their ACC schedule with a .500 record when they host the NC State Wolfpack at Doak Campbell Stadium Saturday afternoon. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on the ACCN. FSU will celebrate its annual Homecoming and Seminole Heritage game and will wear turquoise jerseys and pants for the first time in program history. FSU is 3-0 in Heritage games and 63-12-1 all-time on Homecoming, with 12 consecutive victories. Throughout Native American communities, turquoise represents harmony, friendship and fellowship. The team found out it would wear the jerseys Sunday when defensive back Zae Thomas, a member of the Seminole Tribe of Florida, displayed the uniforms in the team meeting. For more information on FSU’s unique relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida and Seminole Heritage, visit noles.co/Heritage. Florida State (5-5, 3-4 ACC) and NC State will meet for the 45th time, with the Noles leading the series, 27-17, including a 16-6 record in Doak. However, NC State has won the last four matchups with Florida State and six of the last seven meetings. Last year, the 11-21 loss at NC State likely cost the 5-win Seminoles the opportunity to become bowl eligible. Under interim head coach Rick Stockstill, the Seminoles will attempt to win their third consecutive game before closing out the season against the Florida Gators at home on Black Friday afternoon, again with another short week to prepare. The last time FSU won 3 straight games was to open the 2025 season before then losing 7 of the next 9 games. The Wolfpack (4-6, 2-5 ACC) also fired their head coach, Dave Doeren, midseason, ending his 14-year tenure as the winningest coach in Wolfpack history, compiling a 98-74 overall record, including 11 bowl appearances and 10 winning seasons. Former NFL quarterback and former Chuck Amato-coached NC State alum, Phillip Rivers, bringing six years’ experience as a Catholic high school football head coach, was officially hired as the new head coach for NC State earlier this week, effective next season. It has been reported that he will travel to Tallahassee along with the Wolfpack team. Rivers signed a reported five-year deal starting at $3.25 million in total compensation for his first year ($2.4375 million base salary plus $812,500 in supplemental income). This is roughly half of Doeren’s previous $6.375 million salary, making Rivers one of the lowest-paid Power 4 coaches. item.title: Is Texas DB Jelani McDonald a Thorpe Award contender? He's got one last chance to prove it
item.description: Texas Longhorns defensive back Jelani McDonald (4) celebrates a play in the second quarter of the game between Texas Football and Ohio State at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Sept. 12, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) The midterm elections are in the rearview mirror, but there is still some campaigning going on in the state of Texas. This ain't about Gina Hinojosa or James Talarico. Instead, Texas football senior Rasheem Biles recently found himself stumping for the Jelani McDonald ticket. Texas' star linebacker made a proclamation last Saturday about McDonald after the safety had three interceptions in the 22-21 win at LSU . Texas defensive back Jelani McDonald (4) kneels in the end zone ahead of the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) "Jim Thorpe Award, man. Put him on the short list right now," Biles stated afterward. MORE: Subscribe to the Statesman's Texas sports newsletter The three finalists for the Thorpe Award will be announced Tuesday. McDonald wasn't among the 15 national semifinalists for the award that goes to college football's top defensive back, but the award committee can select nonsemifinalists for the final ballot. And with the way McDonald has played over the past month - he was named the Thorpe Award's defensive back of the week Tuesday - perhaps the Waco native has become a late-charging candidate. Texas defensive back Jelani McDonald (4) hypes up the crowd during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) McDonald's 78 tackles are more than all 15 Thorpe Award semifinalists, and only two of the 15 have picked off more passes than McDonald's four. The senior also is playing for a team ranked fifth in this week's College Football Playoff ratings while only four of the 15 semifinalists would be CFP participants if the postseason started today. But enough about Biles' endorsement and the numbers themselves. Does McDonald himself believe he's the best defensive back in college football? "I do," McDonald said. "I've shown a lot." item.title: Michigan Hockey Preview: Top-ranked Wolverines face MSU in rivalry showdown
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 13: Michael Hage #19 of University of Michigan skates with the puck during a game between Penn State and Michigan at Yost Ice Arena on November 13, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Michael Miller/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images For the first time in program history, Michigan Hockey (10-1) has started two seasons in a row by winning 10 of its first 11 games. After sweeping Penn State out of Yost last weekend, the top-ranked Wolverines now turn their sights to ninth-ranked Michigan State (6-3-1) for this weekend’s home-and-home series. Let’s dive into the Spartans first. Michigan State Michigan State limps into Hate Week after a woefully underperforming, two-point weekend against Notre Dame. The Spartans only have one win in their last four games and have struggled to assimilate their new collection of talented players. However, this team is a sleeping giant and cannot be viewed as anything but. Sophomores Anthony Romani (7G, 5A) and Ryker Lee (3G, 7A) have powered the Spartans to start the season, and lead a group that ranks No. 17 in scoring offense. Senior Tommi Männistö only has four points to start the year, but the talented Finn has five points in six career games against the Wolverines. On the blue line, Michigan State’s youth has stolen the spotlight and production. Freshmen Chase Reid (1G, 8A) and Brady Peddle (2A) share the team lead with 15 blocks apiece and make any shot difficult. Reid also leads the unit in scoring. While the production numbers won’t blow anyone away, their defensive prowess and ability to protect the house have helped ease the burden on their freshman goaltender. With elite support, Joshua Ravensbergen has established himself as one of the best goalies in the country. It’s no small task replacing Trey Augustine, but Ravensbergen’s .940 save percentage and 1.86 goals against average have fans moving on faster than a middle school breakup. This is the most talented roster in the country, with 17 NHL Draft picks and an NCAA-record nine first-rounders, and it’s only a matter of time until Adam Nightingale’s squad puts it together. But is that time now? Michigan enters the weekend hotter than fish grease on the offensive end of the ice. Question: How does a team boost its power play percentages? Just score eight power play goals in one series, including seven in one game! Michigan’s power play jumped 13 spots after the series against Penn State and now sits fifth nationally at .326. The Wolverines continue to be led by the two-headed monster of Michael Hage (5G, 21A) and Jayden Perron (13G, 11A). The dynamic duo — who desperately need a nickname to capture this moment of dominance — remain the top points scorers in the country, with Hage leading the country in assists and Perron leading in goals. Moreover, Perron is five points clear of the next leading scorer despite playing three fewer games. This could be a 1-2 Hobey Baker finish for the Wolveri

item.title: 3 key stats to know for Indiana men’s basketball vs Kentucky
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 10: Alex Wilkins #10 and Zoom Diallo #5 of the Kentucky Wildcats high five against the Kansas Jayhawks during the first half in the 2026 State Farm Champions Classic at United Center on November 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indiana men’s basketball is set to take on Kentucky this evening at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana, for the Hoosiers’ second consecutive marquee non-conference matchup. It’s the second game of a four-game series agreed to by both programs to restart the annual rivalry. Indiana fell in Lexington last season and will look to even things up in the Circle City. The Hoosiers are 5-0 while the Wildcats sit at 4-1 with a 20-point loss to Kansas on a neutral court. Here’s a few key stats to keep in mind ahead of the matchup: Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android for coverage of the Hoosiers and all your favorite teams! Kentucky’s opposing 3-point rate: almost 50% Kentucky’s opponents have done a solid job of hurting the Wildcats from deep in the early going of the season. Just under 50% of opponents’ field goal attempts have come from beyond the 3-point line and 34% of those attempts are going in. Volume 3-point shooting helped James Madison keep things close, a 4-8 night from Tre White helped Kansas in a blowout and a 50% shooting performance nearly earned Northern Arizona the upset win over the Wildcats. Indiana’s 3-point shooting isn’t volume-based like last season, the Hoosiers are taking shots from deep at a pretty average amount on the season so far. They’re converting on 35.7% of those attempts, with Bryce Lindsay and Darren Harris performing particularly well on higher volumes. Look for Indiana to get Harris going early and Lindsay to take those shots if they’re open. Markus Burton hasn’t taken too many, but he’s made 7 of the 13 attempts he’s taken so far this season. Indiana’s rising offensive rebounding rate: 42.2% Indiana keeps getting better and better at controlling the glass as the Hoosiers play more games. Which you’d hope for, given how much Darian DeVries stressed it as the team’s identity heading into the season, in practice and in the media. The Hoosiers’ offensive rebounding rate of 42.2% sits at 11th nationally while their rate allowed sits at 84th. Sam Alexis has been particularly effective in going after the glass on the offensive end coming off the bench while Samet Yigitoglu has proven stout as a possession-ender on defense. Kentucky allows offensive rebounds at a slightly below average rate but hasn’t faced a team of Indiana’s size and emphasis up to this point. The Hoosiers will have a chance to impose their will on the Wildcats. Kentucky’s free throw rate: 24.7% Kentucky is the tallest team in college basketball. item.title: Early look at 2027 football roster management
item.description: OXFORD, MISSISSIPPI - OCTOBER 31: Deuce Knight #2 of the Mississippi Rebels reacts after scoring a touchdown during the second half against the Auburn Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Oxford, Mississippi. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’re still staring into the abyss after Ole Miss’ 24-17 loss to Oklahoma on Sunday, you may have missed that Saturday’s game against Wofford will be the official Senior Day for the 2026 season. Although Ole Miss will host the Egg Bowl on Friday, November 27th, they opted not to add pre-game festivities to the Egg Bowl mixer. Probably because transitioning from a pre-game brawl to honoring the outgoing seniors would be a little awkward. However, the crowd 15-20 minutes before the Wofford game (and during the game) will likely be slim, given the following: The season is plodding to a bowl game no one is interested in The students’ last day before Thanksgiving break is today* It’s Wofford It’s 11 AM Egg Bowl is 6 days away *The positive is that none of the shitbirds who throw stuff on the field will be there. That list is a delicious formula for a lot of visible concrete and about 45,000 people, which sucks for those being honored. They deserve better, but it’s unreasonable to ask fans to give a shit about going to the Wofford game. According to Ole Miss, 17 seniors will be honored pre-game, though several players have another year of eligibility left should they choose to use it. For most of those 17, 2026 will be their last year of college football (and football in general). So let’s take a look at which players will not be back in 2027 because they’re out of eligibility, and those who could be back. Players not returning in 2027 (eligibility exhausted) Trinidad Chambliss Horatio Fields Izaiah Hartrup Troy Everett Antonio Kite Jehiem Oatis Keaton Thomas Cedrick Beavers Walker Howard George Hamsley Lucas Carneiro Jonathan Maldonado Raymond Collins Nick Cull John Ross Ashley Anthony Aguirre Patrick Kutas Of those, Chambliss, Fields, Kite, Thomas, Carneiro, and Kutas are starters or started in 2026. Everett, Oatis, Beavers, Maldonado, and Cull were contributors throughout the season. Losing only 6 starters (including the kicker) is of note. Senior starters/contributors who could return in 2027 Johntay Cook II Deuce Alexander Jordan Renaud Jaylon Braxton Blake Purchase Suntarine Perkins Joenel Aguero Traylon Ray Sharif Denson Luke Hasz Edwin Joseph Darrell Gill Jr.* Joshua Dye Delano Townsend Brycen Sanders Isaiah Spencer* Jamarious Brown *Didn’t start or contribute but a transfer of note last year. Pete Golding specifically mentioned Alexander and Perkins as two seniors Ole Miss wants to return, but there are a handful of other guys on the list that they’d love to have back as well. I don’t know what this list’s attrition rate will be, but Ole Miss will ask some to take a pay cut and others will be encouraged to find a new roster or not have another school’s offer match

item.title: Husker Wrestling: All Hands on Deck as Nebraska Sends Guys to Philly and Kearney To Compete
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - MARCH 20: Christopher Minto of the Nebraska Cornhuskers celebrates after defeating Cam Steed of the Missouri Tigers during the Division I Men's Wrestling Championship held at Rocket Arena on March 20, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images This weekend’s schedule for Nebraska wrestling doesn’t grab the national headlines, but it will be a very important weekend for this team. After splitting a pair of duals against Top-10 opponents to start the year, the Huskers will take on #21 Penn Saturday at the Palestra in Philadelphia at Noon on ESPN+. The Quakers have a solid squad with seven ranked wrestlers — including at their first six weight classes. They’ll supply a stiff test for the Huskers who are coming off that 27-6 loss to #2 Oklahoma State last Friday. item.title: Orioles news: The O’s inquired about Hunter Goodman
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 26: Hunter Goodman #15 of the Colorado Rockies celebrates hitting a home run during the third inning against the Chicago White Sox at Rate Field on September 26, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Camden Chatters. We’re less than two weeks away from the expected MLB lockout that will almost certainly put baseball in a deep freeze for months. So far there haven’t been many marquee free agent signings, but a few teams have been active in retooling their roster before they’re indefinitely blocked from making transactions. The Orioles have not been one of them. The Orioles, according to multiple national baseball writers, apparently intend to be busy this offseason. Of course, what they intend to do and what they actually end up doing are two very different things. If the O’s actually are planning on making big changes, I would’ve hoped they would have already started. And yet! We’ve heard rumors linking the Birds linked to several different players, but nothing has materialized, and maybe it never will. The most recent name to come up as a possible O’s target is Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman, a two-time All-Star. The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal writes that the Orioles “were among the clubs to check in on Goodman early in the offseason,” but “the talks failed to advance, and no names were exchanged.” So, uh, that’s probably the end of that, barring one of the teams having a change of heart. It’s understandable that the Orioles were intrigued by Goodman, who led all catchers with 41 home runs this season (technically he hit nine of them as a DH, but let’s not pick nits). The O’s are in dire need of a catching upgrade over Carlos Narváez, preferably someone who can take more than half of the workload behind the plate so that Samuel Basallo can spend more time DHing than catching. Rosenthal notes that Goodman had offseason surgery on his non-throwing shoulder but is expected to be ready by spring training, which almost certainly won’t start in February anyway. The Birds would certainly be shooting high for Goodman, who is one of the best offensive catchers in the game and has three years of team control remaining. Over the last two seasons, Goodman has a .262/.317/.525 line with 72 homers and 179 RBIs. He’s not considered a very good defender, but with a power bat like that, you don’t need to be. The Rockies are likely demanding a hefty return for Goodman, and their asking price apparently was too steep for the Orioles to pay. Once again this appears to be an instance of the Orioles doing their due diligence on a player without ever coming close to actually landing him. Wake me up when something happens for real. item.title: Sheffield United Dealing With Major Right-back Dilemma As Wilder Outlines Transfer Plans
item.description: Sheffield United Dealing With Major Right-back Dilemma As Wilder Outlines Transfer Plans Sheffield United return to Championship action on Saturday afternoon when they welcome Watford to Bramall Lane , with Chris Wilder’s side looking to get back to winning ways following a frustrating defeat before the international break. The Blades had put together an encouraging four-game unbeaten run before travelling to The Valley, but were unable to extend that sequence as they suffered a disappointing 2-1 defeat against Charlton Athletic . It was a frustrating afternoon for United, who will feel they could have taken something from the contest, particularly given their recent improvement in results and performances. However, the international break has provided Wilder and his coaching staff with an opportunity to take stock, address some of the issues that have emerged during the opening months of the campaign and work on improving the fitness levels of several players. There is still plenty of football to be played, and United will be hoping that the additional time on the training ground can help them build some momentum heading into the busy winter period. Their opponents arrive in South Yorkshire in inconsistent form. Watford have recorded two victories, two defeats and a draw across their previous five Championship outings, with their most recent fixture ending in a point at home against Middlesbrough. Team News: Bamford Returns as Seriki Faces Lengthy Spell on Sidelines WATFORD, ENGLAND – APRIL 18: Patrick Bamford of Sheffield United celebrates scoring thier second goal during the Sky Bet Championship match between Watford and Sheffield United at Vicarage Road on April 18, 2026 in Watford, England. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) The biggest talking point surrounding United’s team news is undoubtedly the devastating injury suffered by Femi Seriki. The right-back was introduced from the bench during the defeat against Charlton, only to suffer a serious knee injury moments after entering the action. Initially it did not look good, and subsequent developments have confirmed the worst possible outcome for the young defender. Wilder has revealed that Seriki faces approximately 12 months on the sidelines after undergoing surgery, effectively ending his involvement for the remainder of the campaign. It is a cruel blow for a player who had established himself as an important part of United’s attacking approach. Seriki’s pace, willingness to drive forward and ability to provide an overlapping threat. Patrick Bamford, meanwhile, is available again after recovering from the shoulder problem that had kept him out of action. His return provides Wilder with another attacking option and should offer a welcome boost as United look to improve their goalscoring output. item.title: Chicago Cubs history unpacked — November 20
item.description: Free of charge for the discerning reader. Happy birthday to Sam Fuld, and a mighty host of others. Today in baseball history, in 1952 – Chicago Cubs slugger Hank Sauer is named National League Most Valuable Player by the Baseball Writers Association of America . The Cubs finished in fifth place despite Sauer’s 37 home runs and 121 RBI, and 1987 – Don Zimmer is hired by long-time friend Jim Frey to manage the Chicago Cubs . Zimmer will compile a 265-258 record during his three-plus-year tenure with the Cubs, including a division title in 1989 , and other stories as well. Today in baseball history : 1962 – New York Yankees center fielder Mickey Mantle collects his third American League MVP Award . Mantle, who hit .321 with 30 home runs, also led the AL in walks (122) and slugging percentage (.605), while helping the Yankees to a berth in the World Series against the San Francisco Giants . 1967 – New York Mets pitcher Tom Seaver , who posted a 16-12 record with 170 strikeouts and 2.76 ERA, is named National League Rookie of the Year by the BBWAA . 1969 – San Francisco Giants first baseman Willie McCovey edges New York Mets pitcher Tom Seaver as National League Most Valuable Player . McCovey hit .320 and led the league in home runs (45) and RBI (126), while Seaver posted a 2.21 ERA with 208 strikeouts and a league-leading 25 wins. 1974 – Texas Rangers right fielder Jeff Burroughs , who batted .301 with 25 home runs and a league-leading 118 RBI, wins the American League MVP Award . Oakland teammates Joe Rudi , Sal Bando and Reggie Jackson are the runner-ups. 1984 – Four days after his 20th birthday, New York Mets pitcher Dwight Gooden becomes the youngest player ever to win the National League Rookie of the Year Award . Gooden posted a 17-9 record with a 2.60 ERA and a major league-leading 276 strikeouts. 1984 – Seattle Mariners first baseman Alvin Davis , who hit .284 with 27 home runs and 116 RBI, wins the American League Rookie of the Year Award . Teammate pitcher Mark Langston and Minnesota Twins outfielder Kirby Puckett are the runner-ups. 1985 – New York Yankees first baseman Don Mattingly , who hit .324 with 35 home runs and 145 RBI, easily wins the American League Most Valuable Player Award over Kansas City Royals third baseman George Brett (.335, 30, 103). 1989 – Milwaukee Brewers center fielder Robin Yount edges Ruben Sierra of the Rangers to win his second American League MVP Award . Yount, who won the award as a shortstop in 1982 , becomes only the third player to win MVP awards at two different positions, joining Hank Greenberg and Stan Musial . 1990 – Oakland Athletics outfielder Rickey Henderson edges Cecil Fielder of the Tigers for the American League MVP Award . Henderson hit .325 with 28 home runs and a major league-best 65 stolen bases. 2001 – Seattle Mariners outfielder Ichiro Suzuki becomes only the second rookie in major league history to win the Most Valuable Player Award . item.title: Iowa Hawkeyes Football: Illinois Fighting Illini Game Preview
item.description: IOWA CITY, IA - NOVEMBER 14: Running back Braeden Jackson #22 of the Iowa Hawkeyes goes up the field in the second half against defensive back Jett Goldsberry #3 of the Purdue Boilermakers on November 14, 2026 at Kinnick Stadium, in Iowa City, Iowa. Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images This weekend, the Iowa Hawkeyes travel to Champaign to take on Hawkeye alum Bret Bielema and his University of Illinois Fighting Illini. The Illini are fighting for respectability and bowl positioning while Iowa, in theory, are fighting to keep its slim Playoff hopes alive, but unfortunately, the Playoff Committee doesn’t think much of Iowa . I, like most Hawkeye fans and most fans of most teams, could go on a tirade about how disingenuous and silly the Playoff Committee is, but what would be the point? Their goal is to stir up controversy so people will watch their phony show. In that, I suppose they are successful even if the long-term effects include projecting a lack of legitimacy. The fact of the matter is the only thing the Hawkeyes can do is go out there and win. Everything else is out of their control. 3 Questions Can Iowa Lay on the Style Points? Iowa has dominated its opponents the last three games though the scoreboard may not reflect that. It reflects a dominant defense and the final score has covered the spread, but it is not a 56-0 drubbing which is what most people think of when they think of dominance. It is evident that Kirk Ferentz and Tim Lester want to treat their offense as a defensive weapon. That means long drives that control the clock. In their last three games, the Hawkeyes have largely done that. The time of possession has been: Iowa 36:21, WI 23:39, Iowa 28:13, NU 31:47, Iowa 35:14, PU 24:46. This, of course, is not how you get to 55-0. That usually involves fast drives so that you have more drives which allows you to score more. According to Fourth and Short , Iowa ranks 85th nationally in terms of offensive pace. Interestingly, the Hawkeyes are one of the slowest teams in the country (125th) when trailing. In other words, no matter the situation, Iowa is the tortoise, not the hare. If Ferentz and Lester have their way, expect more of the same against Illinois. It’s not that Iowa won’t take a big play for a quick touchdown, or multiple quick plays for quick touchdowns. It’s that this is not the gameplan. I don’t know what the Playoff Committee looks for besides wins. I don’t know how the Playoff Committee defines dominance. But I am confident that Kirk Ferentz is not going to depart from his way of playing football, and in that respect, he’s right. You try to do things against your basic nature and that’s when bad things happen, like losing, which I am sure will not impress the Playoff Committee. What Makes Illinois Good? Good is relative, but the Illini certainly aren’t a bad team. They’ve got six wins, they beat Oregon and took UCLA to the wire, in California. Yet, statistically they kind of suck. item.title: Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph praises Riley Moss for his resilience and toughness
item.description: DENVER , CO - JANUARY 4: Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph of the Denver Broncos roams the sidelines during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, January 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos have become one of the best franchises in the National Football League when it comes to rewarding their players who perform well. Since the Walton-Penner Family Ownership Group took over several seasons ago, the Broncos have doled out nearly a dozen large contracts to assemble a championship caliber roster. Yesterday, fourth-year cornerback Riley Moss became the most recent player to earn a lucrative multi-year contract extension. While no particulars on guarantees have been provided, the known terms are a four-year deal worth up to $67 million dollars. That’s a shade below $17 million annually, and several million less on average than many thought he would garner on the open market. Yesterday after practice and the news about the extension, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph met with the media and was asked about the importance of getting the deal done. “It’s special. I think it speaks to the Walton-Penner Family Ownership, the GM, and the Head Coach. That’s the program. That’s the plan here to draft, develop and retain. It’s working to obviously maintain and get better each year. That’s the key to this league. Keep your own and find them early and pay them,” stated Joseph. The Broncos moved up in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft to select Moss out of Iowa. As a rookie, it was mostly a learning season for the former Hawkeyes standout. He appeared in 14 games, but most of his action was as a core special teams’ player. He only had 23 defensive snaps that season. Over the next two years, Moss would be a 31-game starter for the Broncos opposite of All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II. Between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, he would log over 1,900 defensive snaps and proved himself to be an important piece in Joseph’s talented secondary. “I’ll start with this; he’s always been very athletic. He’s competitive. To play opposite of Pat Surtain II, that’s a tough job. Outside of Bo Nix on gameday, it’s probably Riley,” Joseph remarked stating who likely has the hardest assignment on a week-to-week basis. In his third season as a starter, Moss has missed some time, but he is performing very well—allowing 223 yards in coverage on 18 catches. Opposing quarterbacks aren’t having much success targeting him at all, completing just 51-percent of passes that go in his direction. Those are all career bests for him. “No one understands his gameday because Pat’s out there at left corner, and they never look at Pat. They do sometimes, but mostly they don’t. They’re trying to find Riley. So that’s a tough job. He’s the perfect personality for that job. Most corners wouldn’t have the resolve to kind of over, and over again just take 12 targ

item.title: 2026 Owners Meetings recap
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 28: Owner Mark Attanasio of the Milwaukee Brewers is presented Commissioner's Trophy by MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred during the Awards Ceremon after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 28, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, major league owners met in New York, a week that sometimes sees interesting league news happen, whether that’s updates on rules, transactions, or other business. But this year, the meetings were dominated by the looming specter of the inevitable lockout, which is set to begin when the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) expires in early December. Labor Negotiations The news is bad on this front. Commissioner Rob Manfred gave a disheartening press conference on Wednesday in which he said, in so many words, that the owners would not ratify a deal without a salary cap. The Players Association, of course, will insist they will not agree — will not even negotiate — if a cap is on the table. Manfred went as far as to hint that they might bring the union in front of the National Labor Relations Board for “refusing to bargain,” and suggested that the political appointees in charge of the NLRB would be friendly to ownership, which is probably true. I’m not a fortune teller, but it looks like the owners are more committed to instituting a salary cap than they have ever been, and the players look to be fully aligned against it, and it seems like a near impossibility that the baseball season will start on time. Threats of legal action before the lockout even begins do not seem like a healthy place to start. Major League Baseball hasn’t lost games because of a labor dispute in over 30 years, since the strike that cancelled the 1994 World Series, but it certainly looks like we’re headed in that direction. Dumb. Manfred also suggested that he’s anti-Thanksgiving in the press conference. Dude is a PR nightmare. Transactions There have been a few big moves in the sport this week, as free agents angle for deals before the work stoppage ends all business and baseball ops bosses make some trades before they can’t anymore. Jake Bauers was one of the first big dominoes of the offseason to fall when he signed with the Red Sox on Friday. Here are a few other notable transactions since then: On Sunday, the Brewers made their first major league move of the offseason when they traded for Ryan Walker from the Giants for minor leaguers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry. Tuesday saw a lot of action as teams had to add players to their 40-man rosters to protect them from the Rule 5 draft; Milwaukee added six players . Also on Tuesday, the Twins’ catcher Ryan Jeffers and the Yankees’ reliever David Bednar accepted qualifying offers and will return to their teams on one-year deals. item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs sit in first place in the AFC West with a 7-2 record, but they cannot afford to let their guard down against the Arizona Cardinals. The team faces a difficult five-week stretch that includes games against top teams like Buffalo, Cincinnati, and San Francisco. A loss to the 3-7 Cardinals would be disastrous for their division hopes. The Chiefs need to treat this game with the same seriousness as any other contest on their schedule. Arizona has suffered from a high number of injuries that have weakened their roster significantly. They currently have 16 players on injured lists, which ties them with the San Francisco 49ers for the most in the NFL. Despite these struggles, the Cardinals still possess skilled players who can make big plays if the Chiefs are not focused. The game takes place on Sunday, November 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City. It is common for teams to underestimate opponents with losing records, but this mindset can lead to costly mistakes. The Chiefs have a five-week meatgrinder coming up, and they need to start stacking wins in November and December. Chiefs linebacker Drue Tranquill noted that the team must focus on winning every game they play. He stated that the message is about stacking wins in November and December, and the team will try to do that on Sunday. The Cardinals have lost their last few games, including a 34-6 defeat to the Rams last weekend. This loss might make the Chiefs feel confident, but confidence can turn into complacency quickly. The Cardinals still have NFL talent on their roster despite the injuries. Tranquill noted that while the roster has suffered many injuries, it still possesses considerable NFL talent. History shows that the Chiefs have dominated this series in the past, leading 10-3-1 all time. However, past success does not guarantee future results, especially when the stakes are high. The Chiefs beat the Falcons 35-13 last week, but that does not mean they are invincible. Every game requires full effort and preparation to avoid an upset. Arizona’s Injury Crisis and Roster Limitations Safety Andrew Wingard and linebacker Jordan Burch were added to injured reserve by the Arizona Cardinals this week. item.title: Walker Kessler finally breaks silence on Stephen A. Smith’s ‘white guys’ criticism of LA Lakers
item.description: Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images Walker Kessler speaks up against Stephen A. Smith for setting up a controversial narrative against the Los Angeles Lakers. Despite the Los Angeles Lakers suffering a shocking 109-97 defeat against the Utah Jazz in their most recent game, they remain one of the best teams in the NBA this season. Evidently, fans see the Lakers among the favourites to win the Western Conference and potentially lift the Larry O’Brien trophy in 2027. However, NBA analyst Stephen A. Smith has been setting up a narrative that it’s impossible for the Lakers to win it all because their three best players are white. Walker Kessler brushes off Stephen A. Smith’s consistent criticism of LA Lakers The three white players in question are Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler. Doncic and Reaves have maintained silence about Smith’s controversial comments. However, Kessler finally shared his thoughts on the same during a recent episode of ‘The Young Man and The Three’ podcast. “I know. I mean, people are gonna say what they’re gonna say. I don’t really care. I’m just gonna be completely honest. I think regardless of if we were white, black, or whatever, we’re just playing basketball,” Kessler said. He added, “At the end of the day, it really doesn’t matter. If you can play this game, it doesn’t matter what you look like.” Instead of getting angry at Smith, Kessler simply wants the Lakers’ basketball skills to do the talking. After all, Smith will be automatically silenced if the Lakers can produce a deep postseason run and ultimately turn it into a championship. item.description: Journalist gives transfer update on €40m PSG star as January window gets closer PSG goalkeeper Lucas Chevalier has not asked to leave the club – even though it’s clear that he’s not getting his starting place back. If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. PSG goalkeeper Lucas Chevalier has not had a nice time at the club. He made a big money move in the summer of 2025, but simply didn’t find the form necessary to keep his place in the team. He was dropped for Matvey Safonov midway through last season, and has since been sitting on the bench. It really feels like his time in Paris is over before it ever really began. A January move has been rumoured repeatedly. Lucas Chevalier has not pushed for PSG departure Claudio Villa/Getty Images According to Olivier Tallaron, a journalist working for Canal+ who was quoted on FootMercato , however, the goalkeeper has not asked to leave the club this winter. It’s not clear what the plans are for Chevalier. After losing his place a little under a year ago he’s really never been given a chance to win it back. Even if he hasn’t asked to leave, there’s no doubt PSG would accept reasonable offers for him. The question is who is going to take a punt on him, especially given he’s getting so few opportunities to prove himself. item.title: When will England play Norway and who could they play in Nations League semi-finals?
item.description: England will play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in March, in a rematch of this summer’s World Cup quarter-final. Jude Bellingham scored twice in Miami as England came from behind to end Norway’s sensational World Cup run back in July. England’s World Cup came to an end following defeat to Argentina in the semi-finals but Thomas Tuchel ’s side are now looking to build on their impressive victory over world champions Spain in Madrid, which saw them top Group A3, by winning the Nations League for the first time. But Erling Haaland ’s team will be out for revenge after their incredible comeback to beat Denmark secured progress to the two-legged Nations League quarter-finals. Norway needed to beat Denmark in Copenhagen to finish as runners-up in Group A4, but found themselves two goals down inside 15 minutes. They fought back, however, with Haaland’s last-minute penalty sending them through to the quarter-finals for the first time. A place in the Nations League Finals, which will be staged in June and at the end of the season, is up for grabs for the winners. There have been reports of the Football Association expressing an interest in hosting the Nations League Finals, which feature the two semi-finals, a third-place match, and the final. Portugal, Italy, the Netherlands and Germany have previously hosted the Finals. When will the Nations League quarter-finals take place? England will travel to Oslo in the first leg before hosting the second leg as they bid to reach the Nations League Finals in June. The two-legged quarter-final will take place during the next international break in late March, with the dates of the two games to be confirmed in due course. First leg: 25-27 March Second leg: 28-30 March When are the Nations League Finals? The Nations League finals are held at the end of the club season and will be played at one venue in June. Portugal, Italy, the Netherlands and Germany have previously hosted the Finals, and there have been reports that England would be interested in staging them should Thomas Tuchel’s side reach the final four. The host country of the Finals is typically involved in the final four, although the Nations League could also allow the FA a test event before hosting Euro 2028 the following summer, with Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland also co-hosts. Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June Who could England play in the semi-finals? Should England progress to the semi-finals, they will play either Jurgen Klopp’s Germany or Belgium, while the other semi-final will see either Spain or France play against Portugal or the Netherlands. Germany impressively thashed Netherlands 6-0 on the final game of the group phase to leapfrog them in the table and top Group A2, while Belgium won 4-1 against Italy to finish runner-up in Group A2 behind France. What teams are still involved in the Nations League? Nations League quarter-finals Spain vs France Norway vs England Netherlands vs Portugal Belgium

item.title: Court Rejects Atiku’s Bid to Tender Fresh Evidence In Suit Seeking Tinubu’s Disqualification
item.description: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice President and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to present fresh evidence in his suit seeking to prevent President Bola Tinubu from contesting the 2027 presidential election over allegations of forgery of his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate. The judge held that the time allowed by law to present evidence in a pre-election suit was 14 days, in line with Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution. Justice Ekwo agreed with Tinubu and the other defendants that allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence would alter the nature of the original case and violate the provisions of the Constitution. In his ruling on Atiku’s application to amend the originating summons in the suit against Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the judge held that the former vice president attempted to mislead the court by claiming that the proposed amendment would not introduce fresh issues. Justice Ekwo said that, after carefully examining the application, the court found that the ADC presidential candidate sought to substitute existing evidence with new evidence which, if allowed, would circumvent Section 285(9) of the Constitution, which requires such evidence to be presented within 14 days. A man walks past the Federal High Court premises in Abuja, on April 22, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) According to the judge, allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence through the back door would amount to a fundamental injustice against the defendants. Meanwhile, following an agreement among the lawyers, the judge fixed December 2 for the hearing of the substantive suit. Atiku had told the court that he needed to make substantial amendments to his case challenging Tinubu’s eligibility to participate in the 2027 presidential election. In the main suit, Atiku and the ADC asked Justice Ekwo to disqualify Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election. They challenged the authenticity of Tinubu’s NYSC discharge certificate submitted to INEC by the APC. The plaintiffs, who sued the president, the APC and INEC as the first to third defendants, respectively, in an originating summons marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, alleged that the APC submitted a forged NYSC discharge certificate belonging to the president to INEC. INEC Headquarters in Abuja. They, therefore, asked the court to compel INEC to remove Tinubu’s name and that of the APC from the list of candidates and political parties for the presidential election. However, Tinubu and the APC, in a joint counter-affidavit filed on September 9, urged the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety for being incompetent, arguing that the plaintiffs lacked the legal right to institute the case. They denied submitting any forged certificate to INEC for either the 2023 or 2027 presidential elections. T
